correctness.rationale: Exact unitary Zak multiplier, geometric sums and two-vector orthogonal projection establish a pointwise global lower bound; equality requires the unique boundary fiber and uniquely selected positive mixing ratio. Strict Cauchy–Schwarz proves positivity for q≥2. Taylor expansion and Riemann sums establish the exact two asymptotic laws. Finite checker independently confirms normalization and limiting equalities for five parameter sets but is not used to justify universal results.

value.rationale: The exact optimally sharp uniform margin is a natural quantitative frame-stability invariant for arbitrary phase and amplitude interference in a two-pole model, with a uniquely worst destructive mixing coefficient. It shows how q=2 oversampling restores a positive worst-case guarantee unavailable at q=1; the sharp weighted-variance near-pole-coalescence law and high-density normalization inform robust sampling design. These are not arbitrary numeric slices or previously available frame-existence restatements.
